A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Wasserstein-based dataset-distillation work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–G support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: V2 reports original classification accuracies, cross-architecture evaluations, ablations, distribution visualizations, and efficiency measurements in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and reports additional sliced-Wasserstein comparisons, feature-layer experiments, and revised cross-architecture and ablation results.

M1.justification: V3 Equations 13–14 use transport-weighted synthetic BatchNorm statistics, whereas v2 Equation 17 specifies standard aggregation. Algorithm 1 now explicitly outputs sample weights, which Section 4.3 says are used in FKD. The barycenter solver, feature-matching objective, and per-class BatchNorm component already existed in v2, making this a limited procedural refinement.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNette, Tiny ImageNet, and ImageNet-1K for image classification and retain the circle/cross distribution illustration. The added metric, feature-layer, and architecture experiments operate within this existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds G-VBSM and SCDD. The previously WMDD-only cross-architecture table gains SRe2L, CDA, and G-VBSM comparisons, and new Table 5 compares WMDD with sliced Wasserstein. The motivating distribution illustration also replaces its Euclidean comparator with MMD. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Cross-architecture evaluation changes from Tiny ImageNet and ImageNet-1K at 10/50 IPC to ImageNet-1K at 50 IPC, adding ViT-Small to the evaluation architectures. New experiments compare Wasserstein variants at 1/10/50 IPC and features from six backbone layers. The ablation design drops the combined CE-plus-Wasserstein condition. The main benchmark protocol remains ResNet-18 classification with top-1 validation accuracy.

E4.justification: V3 adds analyses of feature-layer depth and the accuracy/runtime tradeoff of sliced Wasserstein, plus a reported near-random outcome from directly substituting MMD into WMDD. It revises the transfer study and removes the joint CE-plus-Wasserstein ablation. The existing regularization sweep, t-SNE analysis, and synthetic-image case studies remain, including material moved between the main text and appendices.

E5.justification: V3 explicitly identifies general three-run reporting as mean and standard deviation and newly specifies five repetitions with standard errors for Table 4 ablations. V2 provides a general three-run statement and unlabeled ablation uncertainty values; the PDFs do not explicitly describe adding runs to those earlier experiments. V2 Table 4's metric-comparison uncertainties are omitted from v3 Figure 4.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains the earlier scores but adds baseline results; cross-architecture and ablation entries are replaced, and sliced-Wasserstein and layer-depth findings are added. For example, sliced Wasserstein achieves 58.3% versus WMDD's 59.4% on Tiny ImageNet at 50 IPC. The ImageNet-1K CE-plus-PCBN ablation changes from 37.4 to 36.4 under revised run reporting. WMDD's total runtime changes from 150.39 seconds in v2 Table 6 to 207.53 seconds in v3 Table 3, now exceeding SRe2L's unchanged 194.90 seconds. Revised transfer settings prevent interpreting changed transfer scores as same-protocol gains.

T1.justification: New Appendix B introduces compact-domain, Lipschitz-loss, characteristic-kernel, and RKHS assumptions and derives expected-loss discrepancy bounds using Wasserstein-1 and MMD. It also develops the connection between mean matching and linear-kernel MMD. This adds substantive formal analysis beyond v2's Wasserstein definitions and barycenter-optimization derivations, which are largely retained.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an efficient, scalable distillation method combining Wasserstein barycenter matching in pretrained feature spaces with BatchNorm regularization and strong high-resolution benchmark performance. V3 foregrounds the WMDD and PCBN names, but the abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution and performance claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds an explanation of conflicts between global BatchNorm alignment and class-specific objectives, and qualifies direct MMD comparisons because the methods use different feature-network arrangements. Appendix B explicitly rejects universal Wasserstein superiority and instead discusses practical kernel and scalability constraints. Conversely, v2 Appendix B's explicit discussion of dependence on an in-domain pretrained classifier and possible alternatives is removed.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies ten barycenter iterations and a 20% synthetic-data validation holdout for cross-architecture epoch selection; the PDFs do not establish whether the holdout itself is new. It supplies code and project URLs, replacing v2's release promise and supplementary-ZIP statement. Most Appendix E settings remain unchanged. The explicit random-crop and horizontal-flip description for the metric comparison is omitted.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands its relationship to distribution-matching research: Appendix B distinguishes mean-only DM/CAFE/IDM from characteristic-kernel M3D and discusses their scalability. It also positions PCBN relative to sandwich and compound BatchNorm, adds G-VBSM, SCDD, and sliced-Wasserstein references, and broadens the bias, privacy, and robustness context.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method exposition are extensively rewritten and condensed. Experimental sections are reorganized: efficiency moves from Appendix F to Section 5.4, synthetic-image variety moves from Section 5.7 to Appendix F, and hyperparameter sensitivity becomes a separate section. Terminology, authorship, affiliations, and citation style also change.

P2.justification: The main text switches to a two-column layout with extensively reformatted tables. V3 adds a method diagram and a front-page selection of existing synthetic images, redraws the distribution illustration, and converts the MMD comparison table into a bar chart. Transfer and ablation tables are restructured, while efficiency and image displays are relocated and appendix figures are repacked.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the empirical claims easier to assess through comparative transfer baselines and metric/layer controls, while clarifying weighting and reproducibility details. These gains are moderated by narrower transfer settings, removal of the joint-loss ablation and pretrained-classifier limitation discussion, and lost uncertainty in the MMD plot. The new conditional Wasserstein-1 analysis provides useful context but does not establish superiority of the implemented squared-distance method.
